overall: The AG found the Board violated the OML by discussing a septic variance not on a notice posted 48 hours ahead and by failing to certify OML materials; the agent-appointment topic was not a violation. The complainant's request to redo the hearing was denied because no vote was taken and the topic was later properly posted.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board discussed topics added to an October 2 meeting notice amended less than 48 hours before the meeting, including a septic variance request.
allegations.key_passage: By not including the topic on a notice 48 hours prior to the October 2 meeting, and then discussing the topic anyway, the Board violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board deliberated on a temporary health agent appointment that was added to the notice less than 48 hours before the October 2 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Based on the information before us, we cannot say that Chair Hunt reasonably anticipated the appointment of Brian LaGrasse 48 hours prior to the October 2 meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged members of the Board failed to certify receipt of Open Meeting Law materials within two weeks of taking office.
allegations.key_passage: We find that, due to this failure, the Board violated the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Order that all Board members sign the Open Meeting Law certification form and file it with the Clerk within 30 days of the letter, if not already done.
Order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
remedy_passage: We order all members of the Board to sign a certification form, certifying receipt of the Open Meeting Law and educational materals, and file it with the Clerk within 30 days of the date of this letter, if they have not done so already?
